_comment: Which radar and moment each ramp was measured against, and what the
measurement found. The registry answers only for pairs listed here, so a
ramp cannot reach a legend or a readout without this evidence.
Produced by validation_tests/visual/ramp_coverage.py, which samples every
distinct opaque color in real frames and asks the shipped invert.ts what
each one reads as. 'colors' is matched over distinct; a ramp ships only at
'radar' is the id the app holds, as RADAR_FOLDER in backend/config.py keys
it, and 'folder' is where the frames were read from. 'moment' is the
published prefix, which is what moment_to_prefix() resolves a console
Adding a pair means running the tool and pasting its numbers, not editing

KBBX, KDAX and KMUX publish a reflectivity bar in the same tree (md5 aad5def3, -30 to 80 dBZ, measured 15/15 over 422,055 px on 2026-07-01 frames). It is left out because the console never paints those frames: they are not selectable radars, and the NEXRAD overlay draws the Iowa State nexrad-n0q-wmst WMS layer, which uses the NWS N0Q ramp instead. A ramp with no display path is one more thing to mistake for the right one.

pairs.note: The C-band paints ZDR from a different colormap. Not one of the 253 colors in a million opaque pixels is within tolerance of the X-band ZDR ramp. sscb publishes no colorbar, so its own bounds cannot be read, and the readout stays off.
Same as the C-band's ZDR. Its prefix is PhiDP rather than FilteredPhiDP, which moment_to_prefix() already special-cases, and the colors are a different map.

Measured 2026-11-21 over the ten newest scans. The console opens on this radar and this moment, and it had no measured pair, so the legend and the readout were off on the view the console opens in. Thin frames on a quiet day: 740 opaque pixels carrying 15 of the palette's 17 colors. The palette itself is the band's, established by XEBY and XSCR at 17/17 over 184,158 pixels.

Measured 2026-11-21 over the ten newest scans.

Measured 2026-11-21 over a frame with rain across most of the scan, which is why it reaches 211 of the palette's 56 stops' worth of quantised colors. These four pairs could not be measured before today: the scan route handed every moment a filesystem fetcher on a deployment with no mount, so Velocity, Zdr and PhiDP answered 500 and only Reflectivity, which the archive already held, came back at all.

Measured 2026-11-21 on a nearly clear scan: 74 opaque pixels carrying 17 colors, so this exercises a small part of the table. The table itself is the band's, established by XSCW at 211/211 over 133,663 pixels off a byte-identical colorbar.
Measured 2026-11-21 on a nearly clear scan, 57 opaque pixels. The table is established by XSCW at 235/235 over 133,663 pixels off a byte-identical colorbar.
Measured 2026-11-21 on a nearly clear scan, 74 opaque pixels. The table is established by XSCW as above.

Covered from this radar's own colorbar, not from its frames. The ramp is extracted from <radar>_FilteredPhiDP_colorbar.png, and XSCV publishes that file byte-identical to the other four X-band radars, re-hashed off the AQPI deployment on 2026-11-21 at f75aab2c00ab. So the table here is the one XSCV itself publishes rather than a sibling's borrowed. The frame check is the separate question of whether the frames are painted with it, and it could not run: every FilteredPhiDP frame in the rolling hour is fully transparent, which the filter explains, since it masks PhiDP where the correlation or the signal is low. Run it when there is rain over Coyote Valley.
Covered from this radar's own colorbar at f75aab2c00ab, for the same reason as XSCV above, and with the same frame check outstanding. Run it when there is rain over Santa Cruz.

The only radar that publishes RhoHV at all: the five X-band folders carry Reflectivity, Zdr, FilteredPhiDP and Velocity, and the route answers 404 for RhoHV on every one of them. The C-band publishes no colorbar, and its Zdr and PhiDP already fail against the X-band tables at 0/253 and 0/256, so it paints these from a colormap nothing here has read. Reading RhoHV's needs the renderer's source on the CoSMoS host rather than anything on this side.

shared_colorbars._comment: Radars whose colorbar PNGs are byte-identical to the measured one, so they paint from the same table. md5 prefixes read on 2026-11-21. The C-band publishes no colorbar and so appears nowhere here, however its frames are measured above.
